Committee to Consider Future Possible Use of Historic Town Hall as a Visitor's or
History Center
MISSION

Opportunity Statement: The Inter-Faith Council for Social Services is proceeding with
plans to vacate Historic Town Hall. A recommendation is needed regarding the
future use and occupancy of this building.
Goal: A Historic Town Hall Committee will represent the interests of the Town of
Chapel Hill and Orange County to consider the opportunity to renovate the Historic
Town Hall building at 100 West Rosemary Street as a Visitor's Center, a History
Center, or both for possible occupancy by the Chapel Hill and Orange County Visitor's
Bureau, Chapel Hill Historical Society, and/ or Chapel Hill Museum.
BACKGROUND

In September 2015, the Inter-Faith Council for Social Services relocated its men's
shelter to 1315 Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd. The IFC is moving forward with a request
to construct a new building where its current food pantry stands on 110 W. Main St.
to accommodate the additional community food kitchen services currently being
offered at the IFC’s 100 W. Rosemary St. location. The IFC expects to relocate to the
W. Main Street location in approximately 2-3 years.
On June 27, 2016, the Town received a petition regarding combining the Visitor's
Center and Chapel Hill Museum at the Historic Town Hall facility. The committee will
respond to this petition by considering these uses of Historic Town Hall.
Historic Town Hall is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The Council
previously expressed interest in placing the building under a conservation easement
with an appropriate nonprofit organization.
DECISION POINTS

Determine whether Historic Town Hall is suitable for a Visitor’s Center staffed by the
Orange County Visitor’s Bureau and/or a History Center and home for the Chapel Hill
Historical Society.
DELIVERABLES

 Report of Findings and Recommendation
 Revised Estimate for Renovating Historic Town Hall
POTENTIAL STAKEHOLDERS

 Town of Chapel Hill and Orange County Residents
 Town of Chapel Hill and Orange County Visitors
 County and Town Governments
 Chapel Hill and Orange County Visitor's Bureau
 Chapel Hill History Museum
 Chapel Hill Historical Society

COMMITTEE
COMPOSITION, ROLES,
AND RESPONSIBILITIES

 [1] Committee Chair to lead the committee, represent and liaise with the
Town of Chapel Hill Council; facilitate discussion and decision-making, while
endeavoring to maintain equal opportunity for all members to participate in
discussion; and coordinate Town and County staff support to the committee.
 [8] Committee Members including community members and stakeholders
with an interest in the future use of Historic Town Hall. Committee members
will attend meetings; participate in discussion and decision-making,
endeavoring to maintain equal opportunity for all members to participate in
discussion; represent the interests of the community; and vote on
committee decisions.
 [1] Town of Chapel Hill Staff Project Manager and [1] Orange County Staff
Project Manager will support the committee with direction from the Chair.
Support will include preparing meeting agendas; meeting scheduling and
arrangements; public notification; preparing and providing information and
documents to committee to assist in decision-making; preparing and
disseminating meeting summaries to committee, Chair, and Town and
County management.
TIMEFRAME

 Provide a report and recommendations for the use of Historic Town Hall as a
visitor's and/ or history center to the Council in May 2017.

FACTORS FOR
CONSIDERATION

 Possibility for Visitor's Bureau and Historical Society to Operate in Shared
Facility
 Historic Preservation Requirements for Renovating Building
 Cost of Renovation
 Sustainability and Maintenance Costs
BOUNDARIES OF SCOPE

This committee's charge is to determine whether Historic Town Hall is suitable for a
Visitor's Center and/or History Museum. Ideas for other uses could be identified as
they relate to the consideration of this charge but would not be considered as a part
of this charge.
